what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat several conditions, including flare-ups of multiple sclerosis (MS), certain kidney problems (nephrotic syndrome), inflammation in the eye (ophthalmic diseases), severe skin conditions, joint and muscle problems like rheumatoid arthritis, and certain lung diseases. It works by telling your adrenal glands (small glands near your kidneys) to make more of your body's natural steroids, which helps reduce inflammation and calm down your immune system.
how_to_take: This medicine is a gel that is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneous) or into a muscle (intramuscular). Your doctor or nurse will teach you exactly how to give yourself the injection at home. Always use a new needle each time. Inject into areas like the outer thigh, stomach (avoiding the belly button area), or upper outer arm. Rotate injection sites each time so you do not inject in the same spot twice in a row. Do not inject into skin that is bruised, red, sore, or hard. Gently warm the vial in your hands before use to make the gel easier to draw into the syringe.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your condition and how you respond to treatment. Doses are often given every day, every other day, or several times per week depending on what you are being treated for. For MS flare-ups, a common dose is 80 to 120 units per day for 2 to 3 weeks. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions exactly. Do not change your dose on your own. Your doctor will slowly reduce (taper) your dose before you stop taking it — do not stop suddenly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. If it is close to your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. Keep the vial in its original box to protect it from light. Do not shake the vial vigorously. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used needles and syringes in an approved sharps container — never throw them in the regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who have active infections, chickenpox, measles, or other contagious illnesses, as this medicine can weaken your immune system. Do not receive live vaccines (such as MMR, varicella, or nasal flu vaccine) while taking this medicine without first talking to your doctor. Limit alcohol use, as it can increase the risk of stomach problems and other side effects. Avoid taking aspirin or ibuprofen (like Advil or Motrin) unless your doctor says it is okay, as combining these with this medicine may increase the risk of stomach ulcers. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, or a cough that won't go away; unusual weight gain, swelling in your legs or ankles, or puffiness in your face; high blood sugar symptoms like increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision; severe stomach pain; mental or mood changes like depression, anxiety, or confusion; muscle weakness; vision problems or eye pain; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; or signs of adrenal crisis (a rare but serious emergency) such as extreme tiredness, dizziness, fainting, nausea, and vomiting.
when_it_works: How quickly this medicine works depends on what condition is being treated. For MS flare-ups, some people begin to feel better within a few days, but it may take 2 to 3 weeks for full improvement. For other conditions, it may take several weeks of regular treatment to notice significant benefits. Be patient and continue taking the medicine as prescribed, even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially bone thinning (osteoporosis), high blood pressure, and infections. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless the benefits clearly outweigh the risks. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine can slow growth in children if used for a long time. The doctor will use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time. Patients with diabetes: This medicine can raise blood sugar levels, so monitor your blood sugar more closely and talk to your doctor about any changes in your readings.
